correctness.rationale: For 1<=p<q, gcd(p,q)=1, rational phases generate min(q,n+1) distinct length-n factors in prefix-count chain order. Iterated deletion of first ones and appending them preserves prefix dominance: the one-position vectors obey coordinatewise ordering after every iterate. Each internal phase cut either changes total ones or makes disjoint 01-to-10 moves at positions congruent to the cut. Exactly when the last moved one has rank <=k does T^k identify adjacent factors, equivalent to the final affected index j<=H=floor((kq-1)/p). The residue-class interval gives the deficit B; H is never divisible by q, giving sharp last collision at n=q+H-1. Independently recomputed 15,260 exact counts and 1,204 sharpness/boundary checks using literal cyclic factors and iterated map. Finite tests supplement but do not prove all integers.
